questions.en: Challenge 5. If the techniques mentioned above (or other techniques) could be applied effectively to population-dynamics simulations, this would greatly advance the rigorous computation of the upper and lower bounds (上下限) on the satisfiable/unsatisfiable (SAT/UNSAT) transition point and on other transition points of the K-SAT problem. This would be a very important achievement for theoretical computer science. [Context on the same page, which says what 'the techniques mentioned above' are: 'According to Guerra's work, the exact solution of the 1RSB integral equations would give a rigorous variational bound (printed 上下限, literally "upper and lower bound") on the SAT/UNSAT transition point [9]. Research groups around the world have independently applied population dynamics, including one of us [21,22]. Many numerical simulation schemes in analysis and mathematical physics can give rigorous upper and lower bounds by means of certain techniques (such as interval arithmetic, 区间代数法). The most famous example is the existence of a fixed point of the Feigenbaum operator in the theory of dynamical systems, first proved by O. Lanford; a separate review can be found in [13].' Just before this (PDF pp. 458–459, book pp. 425–426), the article says that statistical-physics predictions for CSPs depend on numerically solving very complex integral equations, the 1RSB cavity-field equations, defined either for a single large instance or for an ensemble. Their solutions are probability distributions. Population dynamics, the only known numerical scheme, needs an initial distribution, and different initial distributions can lead to different fixed points.]

questions.formal_statement:
LITERAL BOOK STATEMENT (Challenge 5, PDF p. 459). The challenge is conditional and reads as a research program. If interval-arithmetic-type techniques 'or other techniques' could be applied effectively to population-dynamics simulations of the 1RSB cavity equations, this would greatly advance the rigorous computation of 上下限 (upper and lower bounds) on the SAT/UNSAT transition point and on other transition points of random K-SAT. The book fixes no K and gives no numerical targets.

NARROWED QUESTION (owner focus). Model: fix k ∈ {4, 5} (the article's K). For n ≥ k and α > 0, let Φ = Φ_k(n, α) be a random k-CNF on n Boolean variables (Ising spins σ_i ∈ {−1, +1}) with m = ⌊αn⌋ clauses. Each clause a independently picks a set ∂a of k distinct variables uniformly at random and a forbidden pattern (J_{ai})_{i∈∂a} ∈ {−1, +1}^k uniformly at random. Clause a is violated iff σ_i = J_{ai} for all i ∈ ∂a. [ASSUMPTION: the article only says that each clause's K variables are chosen at random among the N and that each clause removes one of the 2^K joint values. The uniform forbidden pattern and the exact ensemble (with or without replacement; ⌊αn⌋ or Poisson(αn) clauses) are standard choices I supplied.] Energy: H_Φ(σ) = number of clauses violated by σ, as in the article.

Definition [ASSUMPTION: phrased so that it does not presuppose a limiting threshold for k = 4, 5]: a real u is a rigorous upper bound for the SAT/UNSAT transition of random k-SAT if, for every α > u, lim_{n→∞} P(Φ_k(n, α) is satisfiable) = 0.

Task: for each k ∈ {4, 5}, give an explicit constant u_k and a rigorous proof that u_k is a rigorous upper bound in this sense, with u_k < U_k*. The proof may be analytic, or computer-assisted with every numerical step certified (for example by interval arithmetic). U_k* is the best rigorous upper bound established in the literature before the attempt. [ASSUMPTION: the article gives no baseline values; U_k* must come from the literature check.] No valid u_k can lie below the true threshold. The cavity-method estimates of [15] (the article's 'most precise estimates so far' of the transition point, citing [15,16]) are therefore the conjectured limit of improvement. [ASSUMPTION]

ROUTE NAMED BY THE ARTICLE (context, not a requirement, since the book allows '或者其他技巧'). The article states three things. (1) By Guerra's work, the exact solution of the 1RSB integral equations gives 'a rigorous variational 上下限' on the SAT/UNSAT point [9]. (2) Those solutions are probability distributions, currently obtainable only by population dynamics, which needs an initial distribution and may reach different fixed points. (3) Interval-arithmetic-type techniques give rigorous bounds in other numerical problems (Lanford's Feigenbaum fixed point; review [13]). The article does not say which side of the transition the Guerra bound controls.

[ASSUMPTION, to be verified against [9] and later literature] The Guerra/Franz–Leone interpolation bound is one-sided. For every β > 0, every Parisi parameter m ∈ (0, 1] and every trial 1RSB order parameter (a law on laws of cavity fields): limsup_n (1/n) E log Σ_σ exp(−β H_Φ(σ)) ≤ P_1RSB(α, β, m, trial). Since log Z ≥ −β min_σ H_Φ(σ), this gives liminf_n (1/n) E min_σ H_Φ(σ) ≥ −P_1RSB/β. If this explicit quantity is certified > 0 at density α, then by concentration of min_σ H_Φ the formula Φ is unsatisfiable w.h.p., so α is a rigorous upper bound. On this reading: (a) the route gives only upper bounds on the SAT/UNSAT density, via lower bounds on the ground-state energy; (b) the bound holds for any explicit trial, and solving the 1RSB equations exactly only makes it as tight as possible. A certificate then needs rigorous evaluation of the functional at one explicit trial (for example a finitely supported, population-dynamics-derived one), with controlled truncation of Poisson-degree sums. It does not need certified convergence of population dynamics. (c) Whether [9] as published covers odd K (needed for k = 5) must be checked.

EXCLUDED BY THE NARROWING (but present in the literal challenge): rigorous lower bounds on the SAT/UNSAT point; bounds on 'other transition points' (e.g., the solution-space transitions of Fig. 1, ref. [14]); k other than 4 and 5; exact thresholds; a general rigorous population-dynamics methodology.
questions.solved_means: For the narrowed question, a full solution needs, for each of k = 4 and k = 5, an explicit constant u_k with a complete, checkable rigorous proof that random k-SAT with clause density α > u_k is unsatisfiable with probability tending to 1. The proof may be analytic, or computer-assisted with every numerical step certified (e.g., interval arithmetic with controlled rounding, plus explicit truncation and tail bounds for Poisson-degree sums and trial-measure expectations). u_k must be strictly below the best rigorous upper bound available before the attempt. The article supplies no baseline, so the literature stage should find both the 2009-era bound and the current best. Improving only one of k = 4, 5 is partial success. Following the book's route (certified evaluation of the Guerra/Franz–Leone 1RSB variational bound at an explicit, e.g. population-dynamics-derived, trial order parameter) addresses the book's methodological challenge directly. An improvement by other rigorous means settles the narrowed numerical question but bears only partly on the book's program. Not required: matching lower bounds, exact thresholds, bounds on clustering/condensation or other transitions, or other k. The full literal Challenge 5 would further need a general rigorous (validated-numerics) treatment of population dynamics, giving rigorous upper and lower bounds on the SAT/UNSAT point and other transition points.

references: [9] Franz S, Leone M. Replica bounds for optimization problems and diluted spin systems Journal of Statistical Physics, 2003, 111: 535-564. (Cited for the Guerra-type rigorous variational bound on the SAT/UNSAT point.)
Guerra's work: named in the text as the source of the rigorous variational bound. It has no separate entry in the reference list; the article cites [9] for it.

[13] Koch H, Schinkel A, Wittwer P. Computed-assisted proofs in analysis and programming in logic: a case study. SIAM Review, 1996, 38: 565-604. ('Computed-assisted' as printed. Cited as a review of rigorous computer-assisted bounds via interval-arithmetic-type techniques.)

O. Lanford's first proof that the Feigenbaum operator has a fixed point: named in the text as the most famous example of rigorous bounds from numerical schemes. No reference entry; see the review [13].

[15] Mertens S, Mézard M, Zecchina R. Threshold values for random K-SAT from the cavity method. Random Structures Algorithms, 2006, 28: 340-373. (Cited for the most precise SAT/UNSAT threshold estimates and for predictions that rest on numerically solving the 1RSB equations.)

[16] Mézard M, Parisi G, Zecchina R. Analytic and algorithmic solutions of random satisfiability problems. Science, 2002, 297: 812-815. (Cited alongside [15] for the threshold estimates, the 1RSB cavity integral equations, and Survey Propagation.)
[21] Zhou H J. On the T→0 mean-field population dynamics approach for the random 3-satisfiability problem. Phys Rev E, 2008, 77: 066102. (Population dynamics for the 1RSB equations.)

[22] Zhou H J. Boltzmann distribution of free energies in a finite-connectivity spin glass system and the cavity approach. Frontiers of Physics in China, 2007, 2: 238-250. (Population dynamics / cavity approach.)

[14] Krzakala F, Montanari A, Ricci-Tersenghi F, Semerjian G, Zdeborová L. Gibbs states and the set of solutions of random constraint satisfaction problems. Proc Nat Acad Sci USA, 2007, 104: 10318-10323. (Cited for the series of solution-space phase transitions, i.e. the 'other transition points'; outside the narrowed focus.)
output.summary: This short perspective by Alava, Aurell and Zhou presents the spin-glass view of constraint satisfaction problems such as random K-SAT and poses five challenges: understanding focused stochastic local search, reconciling the rugged spin-glass energy-landscape picture with the success of local search, explaining why Survey Propagation fails very close to the SAT/UNSAT point, finding efficient certificates of unsatisfiability, and obtaining computer-assisted rigorous bounds. The owner-selected Challenge 5 (PDF p. 459) proposes making population-dynamics solutions of the 1RSB cavity equations rigorous with interval arithmetic or other techniques, building on the Guerra/Franz–Leone variational bound [9], so as to compute rigorous bounds on the SAT/UNSAT and other transition points; here it is narrowed to certified improved upper bounds on the random 4-SAT and 5-SAT satisfiability thresholds.

questions.best_known: As of 2026-10-15, no checked source supplies the requested certified improvements for both k=4 and k=5. The explicit upper-bound benchmarks located in refereed literature remain the classical bounds commonly reported as 10.23 and 21.33: the Achlioptas–Peres table, the 2009 handbook, and Friedrich et al. (2017) corroborate this provenance. These rounded entries must not be treated as exact U_k*: Kirousis et al., Theorem 2, already bounds the transition by the positive root R_k of (1−2^(−k))^R_k[2−exp(−kR_k/(2^k−1))]=1. Floating-point evaluation gives approximately 10.22455 and 21.32280, illustrating why merely beating the printed decimals would not establish novelty. Lelarge–Oulamara supplies an applicable variational framework, but no new numerical pair.
questions.gap: Missing is an explicit pair below the strongest underlying classical bounds, with certified evaluation and a complete proof for independent uniformly signed, distinct-variable clauses with floor(αn) clauses. The 9.931/21.117 cavity values are predictions. Large-k threshold theorems do not cover 4 or 5; the 2026 k=3 and threshold-existence claims do not claim this pair. An energetic warning functional still requires a checked derivation from a valid interpolation theorem, finite-temperature or finite-y control, concentration, and model transfers. The broader literal Challenge 5 additionally includes lower bounds, other transitions, and validated population dynamics; related progress does not resolve that program. This is a dated literature-search verdict, not a proof of openness.

attack.rationale: A four-hour attempt can plausibly produce a checkable finite-trial certificate or a counterexample to a proposed analytic step; a complete improved threshold pair is speculative. Recheck novelty against the underlying classical bounds rather than their rounded table entries, and distinguish floating-point evidence, certified functional inequalities, and threshold theorems throughout. These are proposed attack deliverables; this literature check produced no new threshold certificate.

claims.statement: For k=4 with a4=249/25<10.23 and k=5 with a5=1057/50<21.33, random k-SAT with floor(ak*n) independent clauses, uniformly distinct variable sets within clauses and independent fair signs is unsatisfiable with probability tending to one. The mathematical proof is notes/PROOF.md; commands reproduce its numerical premises, not its universal quantifiers.

For every k>=2, alpha>0, n>=k, finite warning law rho supported in [0,1), T>=1 and y>0, the functional in notes/PROOF.md satisfies -(y/n) E[min violations in the repeated-variable Poisson(alpha*n) model] <= Psi_T+T*exp(-y). identified_counterpart.formal_statement:
LITERAL BOOK STATEMENT (Challenge 5, PDF p. 459). The challenge is conditional and reads as a research program. If interval-arithmetic-type techniques 'or other techniques' could be applied effectively to population-dynamics simulations of the 1RSB cavity equations, this would greatly advance the rigorous computation of 上下限 (upper and lower bounds) on the SAT/UNSAT transition point and on other transition points of random K-SAT. The book fixes no K and gives no numerical targets.

NARROWED QUESTION (owner focus). Model: fix k ∈ {4, 5} (the article's K). For n ≥ k and α > 0, let Φ = Φ_k(n, α) be a random k-CNF on n Boolean variables (Ising spins σ_i ∈ {−1, +1}) with m = ⌊αn⌋ clauses. Each clause a independently picks a set ∂a of k distinct variables uniformly at random and a forbidden pattern (J_{ai})_{i∈∂a} ∈ {−1, +1}^k uniformly at random. Clause a is violated iff σ_i = J_{ai} for all i ∈ ∂a. [ASSUMPTION: the article only says that each clause's K variables are chosen at random among the N and that each clause removes one of the 2^K joint values. The uniform forbidden pattern and the exact ensemble (with or without replacement; ⌊αn⌋ or Poisson(αn) clauses) are standard choices I supplied.] Energy: H_Φ(σ) = number of clauses violated by σ, as in the article.

Definition [ASSUMPTION: phrased so that it does not presuppose a limiting threshold for k = 4, 5]: a real u is a rigorous upper bound for the SAT/UNSAT transition of random k-SAT if, for every α > u, lim_{n→∞} P(Φ_k(n, α) is satisfiable) = 0.

Task: for each k ∈ {4, 5}, give an explicit constant u_k and a rigorous proof that u_k is a rigorous upper bound in this sense, with u_k < U_k*. The proof may be analytic, or computer-assisted with every numerical step certified (for example by interval arithmetic). U_k* is the best rigorous upper bound established in the literature before the attempt. [ASSUMPTION: the article gives no baseline values; U_k* must come from the literature check.] No valid u_k can lie below the true threshold. The cavity-method estimates of [15] (the article's 'most precise estimates so far' of the transition point, citing [15,16]) are therefore the conjectured limit of improvement. [ASSUMPTION]

ROUTE NAMED BY THE ARTICLE (context, not a requirement, since the book allows '或者其他技巧'). The article states three things. (1) By Guerra's work, the exact solution of the 1RSB integral equations gives 'a rigorous variational 上下限' on the SAT/UNSAT point [9]. (2) Those solutions are probability distributions, currently obtainable only by population dynamics, which needs an initial distribution and may reach different fixed points. (3) Interval-arithmetic-type techniques give rigorous bounds in other numerical problems (Lanford's Feigenbaum fixed point; review [13]). The article does not say which side of the transition the Guerra bound controls.

[ASSUMPTION, to be verified against [9] and later literature] The Guerra/Franz–Leone interpolation bound is one-sided. For every β > 0, every Parisi parameter m ∈ (0, 1] and every trial 1RSB order parameter (a law on laws of cavity fields): limsup_n (1/n) E log Σ_σ exp(−β H_Φ(σ)) ≤ P_1RSB(α, β, m, trial). Since log Z ≥ −β min_σ H_Φ(σ), this gives liminf_n (1/n) E min_σ H_Φ(σ) ≥ −P_1RSB/β. If this explicit quantity is certified > 0 at density α, then by concentration of min_σ H_Φ the formula Φ is unsatisfiable w.h.p., so α is a rigorous upper bound. On this reading: (a) the route gives only upper bounds on the SAT/UNSAT density, via lower bounds on the ground-state energy; (b) the bound holds for any explicit trial, and solving the 1RSB equations exactly only makes it as tight as possible. A certificate then needs rigorous evaluation of the functional at one explicit trial (for example a finitely supported, population-dynamics-derived one), with controlled truncation of Poisson-degree sums. It does not need certified convergence of population dynamics. (c) Whether [9] as published covers odd K (needed for k = 5) must be checked.

EXCLUDED BY THE NARROWING (but present in the literal challenge): rigorous lower bounds on the SAT/UNSAT point; bounds on 'other transition points' (e.g., the solution-space transitions of Fig. 1, ref. [14]); k other than 4 and 5; exact thresholds; a general rigorous population-dynamics methodology.

The article supplies no baseline, so the literature stage should find both the 2009-era bound and the current best. Improving only one of k = 4, 5 is partial success. An improvement by other rigorous means settles the narrowed numerical question but bears only partly on the book's program. Not required: matching lower bounds, exact thresholds, bounds on clustering/condensation or other transitions, or other k. The full literal Challenge 5 would further need a general rigorous (validated-numerics) treatment of population dynamics, giving rigorous upper and lower bounds on the SAT/UNSAT point and other transition points.

identified_counterpart.formal_statement:
LITERAL BOOK STATEMENT (Challenge 5, PDF p. 459). The challenge is conditional and reads as a research program. If interval-arithmetic-type techniques 'or other techniques' could be applied effectively to population-dynamics simulations of the 1RSB cavity equations, this would greatly advance the rigorous computation of 上下限 (upper and lower bounds) on the SAT/UNSAT transition point and on other transition points of random K-SAT. The book fixes no K and gives no numerical targets.

NARROWED QUESTION (owner focus). Model: fix k ∈ {4, 5} (the article's K). For n ≥ k and α > 0, let Φ = Φ_k(n, α) be a random k-CNF on n Boolean variables (Ising spins σ_i ∈ {−1, +1}) with m = ⌊αn⌋ clauses. Each clause a independently picks a set ∂a of k distinct variables uniformly at random and a forbidden pattern (J_{ai})_{i∈∂a} ∈ {−1, +1}^k uniformly at random. Clause a is violated iff σ_i = J_{ai} for all i ∈ ∂a. [ASSUMPTION: the article only says that each clause's K variables are chosen at random among the N and that each clause removes one of the 2^K joint values. The uniform forbidden pattern and the exact ensemble (with or without replacement; ⌊αn⌋ or Poisson(αn) clauses) are standard choices I supplied.] Energy: H_Φ(σ) = number of clauses violated by σ, as in the article.

Definition [ASSUMPTION: phrased so that it does not presuppose a limiting threshold for k = 4, 5]: a real u is a rigorous upper bound for the SAT/UNSAT transition of random k-SAT if, for every α > u, lim_{n→∞} P(Φ_k(n, α) is satisfiable) = 0.

Task: for each k ∈ {4, 5}, give an explicit constant u_k and a rigorous proof that u_k is a rigorous upper bound in this sense, with u_k < U_k*. The proof may be analytic, or computer-assisted with every numerical step certified (for example by interval arithmetic). U_k* is the best rigorous upper bound established in the literature before the attempt. [ASSUMPTION: the article gives no baseline values; U_k* must come from the literature check.] No valid u_k can lie below the true threshold. The cavity-method estimates of [15] (the article's 'most precise estimates so far' of the transition point, citing [15,16]) are therefore the conjectured limit of improvement. [ASSUMPTION]

ROUTE NAMED BY THE ARTICLE (context, not a requirement, since the book allows '或者其他技巧'). The article states three things. (1) By Guerra's work, the exact solution of the 1RSB integral equations gives 'a rigorous variational 上下限' on the SAT/UNSAT point [9]. (2) Those solutions are probability distributions, currently obtainable only by population dynamics, which needs an initial distribution and may reach different fixed points. (3) Interval-arithmetic-type techniques give rigorous bounds in other numerical problems (Lanford's Feigenbaum fixed point; review [13]). The article does not say which side of the transition the Guerra bound controls.

[ASSUMPTION, to be verified against [9] and later literature] The Guerra/Franz–Leone interpolation bound is one-sided. For every β > 0, every Parisi parameter m ∈ (0, 1] and every trial 1RSB order parameter (a law on laws of cavity fields): limsup_n (1/n) E log Σ_σ exp(−β H_Φ(σ)) ≤ P_1RSB(α, β, m, trial). Since log Z ≥ −β min_σ H_Φ(σ), this gives liminf_n (1/n) E min_σ H_Φ(σ) ≥ −P_1RSB/β. If this explicit quantity is certified > 0 at density α, then by concentration of min_σ H_Φ the formula Φ is unsatisfiable w.h.p., so α is a rigorous upper bound. On this reading: (a) the route gives only upper bounds on the SAT/UNSAT density, via lower bounds on the ground-state energy; (b) the bound holds for any explicit trial, and solving the 1RSB equations exactly only makes it as tight as possible. A certificate then needs rigorous evaluation of the functional at one explicit trial (for example a finitely supported, population-dynamics-derived one), with controlled truncation of Poisson-degree sums. It does not need certified convergence of population dynamics. (c) Whether [9] as published covers odd K (needed for k = 5) must be checked.

EXCLUDED BY THE NARROWING (but present in the literal challenge): rigorous lower bounds on the SAT/UNSAT point; bounds on 'other transition points' (e.g., the solution-space transitions of Fig. 1, ref. [14]); k other than 4 and 5; exact thresholds; a general rigorous population-dynamics methodology.

The article supplies no baseline, so the literature stage should find both the 2009-era bound and the current best. Improving only one of k = 4, 5 is partial success. The full literal Challenge 5 would further need a general rigorous (validated-numerics) treatment of population dynamics, giving rigorous upper and lower bounds on the SAT/UNSAT point and other transition points.
